# Verification record 2026-10-10

<!-- Generated by `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs render` from 2026-10-10.json; do not edit. -->

**Verification is evidence, not a support guarantee.** This record is the result of one full nightly run of the [compatibility matrix](../cells/COMPATIBILITY.md) at commit `1af6a1c1cfac95827b1cdac9f9ae092d8dc5b033`, with each render backend checked separately. The machine-readable record is [2026-10-10.json](2026-10-10.json); `verifiedRanges` in [seed.json](../seed.json) is derived from the records (`node design/compatibility/verification.mjs ranges`), and `validate.mjs` checks that they agree.

**Rendering: software (GPU profile `software`).** Software rendering: no GPU took part. WebGL ran on ANGLE over SwiftShader and WebGPU on Dawn over SwiftShader's Vulkan device, a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true). It counts as verification; a run on a real GPU (run-cells.mjs --gpu hardware) can be added later as extra evidence.

Rule: A tuple (React adapter, exact React, Pixi adapter, exact pixi.js) is verified on a render backend when its cell passed on that backend in this record (every command, every conformance scenario and the render check) and every boundary probe and every negative case of this record behaved as expected. A run on the expected-blank-render list (adapterMatrix.expectedBlankRender) that failed exactly as listed is not a failure, but verifies nothing. Each tuple lists every backend it is verified on; backends are never inferred from each other.

## Run

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build --force`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs pack --out <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --tier nightly --patches all --cell <a third of the cells> --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs   (three shards in parallel)`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs probes --tier nightly --work <work>`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --negative --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs data --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs`

- Tier: nightly with `--patches all` (184 cells: every React adapter at its minimum and latest audited patch x the newest audited patch of every Pixi 8 minor and pixi.js 7.4.2 and 7.4.3), a superset of the scheduled nightly's 115 cells. Render backends: WebGL and WebGPU (`adapterMatrix.tiers.nightly.renderers`); Pixi 7 cells WebGL only.
- Commit: the merge of main (PR #67, the JSX-order insert fix and the pixi.filter-children scenarios) into the issue-17 branch. An earlier full run at 3946ab4, before that merge, had the same per-backend outcome (WebGL 184/184, WebGPU 104/168 with the same 64 blank-canvas failures); it is superseded by this one.
- Fresh: a new work directory, packages rebuilt with `pnpm build --force`, tarballs packed from that build, `--no-cache` (no verdict reused), CI=true. The npm download cache was shared (registry tarballs are integrity-checked).
- Three cell shards ran in parallel on 4 vCPUs with the probes, then the negative cases and the data-only probes. No test timed out and no failure was retried.
- Commits after this one change documentation, generated tables, the verification tooling and comments only; `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs compare --date 2026-10-10 --tarballs <fresh pack>` shows whether a later commit packs the same code (Markdown and build logs aside).
- Reclassified on 2026-10-10 with `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs refresh` (no cell re-run) after the owner ruled that WebGPU is verified per version: the 64 WebGPU runs of pixi.js 8.2.6 to 8.9.2 match the expected-blank-render entry `pixi8-webgpu-blank-before-8.10-software` exactly (every conformance scenario passed; renderer webgpu; canvas and extract [0,0,0,0]; screenshot not red), so they are recorded as expected blank renders, unverified. The runner of this run, before that list existed, reported them as failures; their read-backs, scenario counts and render-check results are kept as recorded.

## Findings

- WebGL: all 184 cells passed (every command, every conformance scenario, the render check).
- WebGPU: 104 of 168 Pixi 8 cells passed and are verified on WebGPU: pixi.js 8.10.2 to 8.22.0 with every React adapter and patch. The other 64 are every React adapter and patch (8 each) on pixi.js 8.2.6, 8.3.4, 8.4.1, 8.5.2, 8.6.6, 8.7.3, 8.8.1 and 8.9.2: Pixi created a WebGPU renderer and every conformance scenario passed, but the render check failed: the screenshot of the canvas is the white page ([255,255,255,255]) instead of the red rectangle, and the canvas copy and Pixi's extract read [0,0,0,0]. They are on the expected-blank-render list (adapterMatrix.expectedBlankRender): expected blank render, unverified.
- The blank render does not depend on the React adapter; pixi.js 8.10.2 and every later minor render on the same adapter, so the cause appears to be in pixi.js before 8.10. Not narrowed below 8.9.2 to 8.10.2 (only each minor's newest audited patch runs); not checked on a real GPU.
- Rendering was software throughout (no GPU in the machine): WebGL on ANGLE/SwiftShader, WebGPU on SwiftShader's fallback adapter. Owner ruling: software rendering counts as verification; a real-GPU record can be added as extra evidence.
- Boundary probes: 44 of 44 passed (pixi-8.5.0 by failing exactly as the audit recorded; no API or type drift). Incompatible pairs: 6 of 6 rejected as expected.

## Data only, not verified

**Data only, not verified: these results are never verification, never enter verifiedRanges and never change a peer range.**

Data-only probes (issue 17). Each probe installs the packed adapters beside a React or pixi.js the adapter does not declare, ignoring peers, and records what every cell command does. The adapters' environment checks are bypassed in the conformance run only (cell.json dataOnly.bypassEnvironmentCheck), so the suite shows what would happen past them. Results are data, never verification: nothing here enters verifiedRanges or changes a peer range.

### pixi7-earlier-releases

The Pixi 7 adapter on pixi.js releases below its 7.4.2 floor: the highest patch of 7.0 to 7.3, and 7.4.0 (7.4.1 was never published to npm).

- pixi.js 7.4.1: not run, absent from the npm registry's version list and time map: there is nothing to install.

### react18-earlier-minors

The React 18 adapter on React 18.0, 18.1 and 18.2, each with the react-reconciler released with it (npm peers: 0.27.0 react ^18.0.0, 0.28.0 react ^18.1.0, 0.29.0 react ^18.2.0; 0.29.2, which the adapter depends on, declares react ^18.3.1). ### Data-only findings

- React 18.0.0, 18.1.0 and 18.2.0 with the reconciler released with each (0.27.0, 0.28.0, 0.29.0, installed through an npm override; npm-ls confirms the swap): the strict peer check rejects the install (tree: react and react-dom invalid against the adapter's exact 18.3.1 peer), and the adapter's checkEnvironment() rejects them (UNSUPPORTED_TUPLE); its REACT18.reconciler still reports the 0.29.2 it was built for. Past the check, with the harness lending act from react-dom/test-utils (React.act exists from 18.3), the whole conformance suite passed on pixi.js 7.4.3 (WebGL) and 8.22.0 (WebGL and WebGPU) with no host-config failure: the 0.27/0.28/0.29.0 reconcilers accept the host config the React 18 adapter passes. Types pass with @types/react 18.3.31.
- pixi.js 7.4.0: the adapter's entry fails to import in plain Node ('Worker is not defined', a pixi.js 7.4.0 module-scope dependency on a browser global); in Chromium, past checkEnvironment(), the whole suite passes with React 18.3.1 and 19.3.0; types pass.
- pixi.js 7.3.3: imports in Node (rejected only by checkEnvironment()), types pass, and the whole suite passes in Chromium with React 18.3.1 and 19.3.0.
- pixi.js 7.2.4: the suite passes in Chromium with both Reacts; types fail only because two @ts-expect-error directives of the Pixi 7 type consumer are unused (the 7.4 declarations the consumer pins reject those props; 7.2's accept them).
- pixi.js 7.1.4 and 7.0.5: the adapter cannot load. pixi.js 7.1 does not export HTMLText, and 7.0 does not export the filters (AlphaFilter, BlurFilter, ColorMatrixFilter, DisplacementFilter, FXAAFilter, NoiseFilter) or HTMLText from its root, which the adapter's entry imports by name: Node import and the browser build fail, so no conformance scenario ran. Types also fail (consumer.pixi7.tsx Sprite props).
- pixi.js 7.4.1 was never published to npm (absent from the registry's versions and time map), so nothing ran for it.
